items.answer: Location awareness in the Majuli virtual reality (VR) Tour case study was identified during contextual inquiry (CI) as an issue for users exploring a large space, and a possible resolution was to add a location awareness feature, later to be converted into functional requirements during system design.

Interaction in immersive environments is broadly categorized into object interaction, navigation, and interaction for system control, where object interaction means selection and manipulation of objects that are part of the virtual environment, navigation means moving from one point to another in the virtual environment, and interaction for system control means interaction required to change system-related settings.
Hand selection techniques for virtual objects include virtual hand, go-go, prism, and intent-driven selection.
Object manipulation is the modification of an object's properties such as position, orientation, scale, shape, color, texture, behavior, and others, and it typically follows selection of the object.

Three-dimensional (3D) widgets are a simple indirect manipulation technique in which controls are placed directly in the 3D scene with virtual objects, and manipulating a widget manipulates the associated virtual object.

Marker-based augmented reality (AR) applications use markers placed in the environment to trigger an augmented experience, and when a device detects a marker, the desired digital content appears at that marker's position in the real-world view.

questions.question: What is the goal of navigation in a virtual world?
options: To convert surfaces into triangular meshes
To move the user from one point to another
To align the real and virtual worlds
To create a map of the real environment
questions.explanation: Navigation in a virtual world aims to move the user from one point to another, which corresponds to changing the user's field of view or viewpoint.

questions.question: What two parts make up the movement involved in navigation in a virtual world?
options: Locomotion and translational movement
Travel and exploration
Travel and wayfinding
Wayfinding and search
questions.explanation: The movement involved in navigation has two parts: the travel part and the wayfinding part.

data.text: The goal of navigation in a virtual world is to move a user from one point to another by changing their viewpoint. This movement is composed of two parts: the travel part and the wayfinding part.
points: Navigation in a virtual world moves the user from one point to another.
Navigation movement has two parts: the travel part and the wayfinding part.

questions.question: In navigation, what does the travel part, also called locomotion, refer to?
options: The actual movement between two locations
The creation of the virtual environment
The rendering of objects in the virtual environment
The planning of how to reach a destination
questions.explanation: The travel part of navigation is the motor component and refers to the actual movement between two locations.

questions.question: What are locomotion techniques, or travel techniques, used to do?
options: Let a user travel from one place to another and perceive that travel has taken place
Let a user plan a route without moving in the virtual world
Let a user render a virtual scene from a fixed position
Let a user create objects in the virtual environment
questions.explanation: Locomotion techniques are techniques employed to let a user travel in a virtual world from one place to another and to perceive that travel has taken place.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the three ways travel in navigation can be done?
options: Exploration changes the viewpoint continuously, search has no explicit goal, and maneuvering moves around to see, learn, or explore.
Exploration has no explicit goal or target point, search moves to a specified target location, and maneuvering uses short, precise movements.
Exploration moves to a specified target location, search has no explicit goal, and maneuvering uses continuous control of direction and speed.
Exploration uses short, precise movements, search moves around to see, learn, or explore, and maneuvering moves to a specified target location.
questions.explanation: Travel can be done by exploration, which has no explicit goal, search, which moves to a specified target, or maneuvering, which comprises short, precise movements.

questions.question: Which four broad types of locomotion techniques are used to accomplish travel in navigation?
options: Full gait, partial gait, gait negation, and spatial steering
Walking-based, steering-based, selection-based, and manipulation-based
Exploration, search, maneuvering, and wayfinding
Physical steering, selection-based, manipulation-based, and panoramic video
questions.explanation: Travel in navigation can be accomplished using walking-based, steering-based, selection-based, and manipulation-based locomotion techniques.

questions.question: Which broad locomotion technique type involves navigating by manipulating certain things?
options: Steering-based locomotion
Selection-based locomotion
Manipulation-based locomotion
Walking-based locomotion
questions.explanation: Manipulation-based locomotion involves navigating by manipulating certain things, while object manipulation may not be involved in walking-based, steering-based, or selection-based locomotion.

data.text: Locomotion is the motor component of navigation referring to actual movement between locations. Locomotion techniques let users travel and perceive that travel in a virtual world through exploration, search, or maneuvering. There are four broad types of locomotion: walking-based, steering-based, selection-based, and manipulation-based. While manipulation-based locomotion involves manipulating objects, navigation usually involves no object manipulation.
points: Locomotion is the motor component of navigation referring to actual movement between locations.
Locomotion techniques let users travel and perceive that travel in a virtual world.
Travel can be done through exploration, search, or maneuvering.
Locomotion techniques are categorized into walking-based, steering-based, selection-based, and manipulation-based types.
Manipulation-based locomotion involves manipulating objects, but navigation usually involves no object manipulation.

questions.question: Walking-based locomotion is based on which input from the physical world?
options: Manipulated virtual objects
Continuous steering controls
The user's physical walking or movement
Selected target locations
questions.explanation: Walking-based locomotion maps physical walking or movement in the physical world to corresponding movement in the virtual environment.

questions.question: Which of the following is a category of walking-based locomotion?
options: Full gait
Spatial steering
Selection-based travel
Manipulation-based travel
questions.explanation: Walking-based locomotion is divided into full gait, partial gait, and gait negation techniques.

questions.question: Why is physical walking restricted in full-gait techniques?
options: Because the user must walk in place to avoid changing position
Because specialized pressure sensors are needed to detect the walking pattern
Completely free walking is impractical, so restricted physical walking is mapped to potentially unlimited virtual movement
Because natural lateral movement is difficult to map to focused virtual movement
questions.explanation: Although actual walking is the most natural form of travel, completely free walking is not practical, so physical walking is limited while virtual movement can be much larger.

questions.question: In a partial gait technique, how is virtual movement created?
options: The user's actual walking in a bounded physical space is translated to virtual movement
The user's continuous direction and speed control a virtual vehicle
The user's walking-in-place pattern is mapped to virtual movement using specialized devices
The user's lateral movement is canceled by a fixed-position setup
questions.explanation: In partial gait techniques, the user walks in place without changing physical position, and specialized input devices map that walking pattern to movement in virtual space.

questions.question: Why does a gait-negation setup cancel the user's lateral movements?
options: To make full gait the most natural way to travel
Natural lateral walking is hard to map to focused virtual movement, so removing it helps the system infer intended travel
To map a single-place walking pattern to different virtual walking types
To let the user change physical position while moving in the virtual environment
questions.explanation: Gait-negation setups cancel lateral movement and keep the user's physical position fixed, making it easier for the system to understand the intended virtual movement.

data.text: Walking-based locomotion maps physical movement in the real world to movement in a virtual environment and is categorized into full gait, partial gait, and gait negation. Full gait translates real-world walking into virtual movement, although physical walking is often restricted. Partial gait involves walking in place with specialized devices, while gait negation uses specialized setups to cancel lateral movements to map the user's intended navigation.
points: Walking-based locomotion maps physical movement in the real world to movement in a virtual environment.
These techniques are broadly divided into full gait, partial gait, and gait negation.
Full gait techniques translate real-world walking into virtual movement, though physical walking is often restricted.
Partial gait involves walking in place with specialized devices, while gait negation uses specialized setups to cancel lateral movements.

questions.question: Which feature defines steering-based navigation?
options: Instant movement to a chosen target
Selection of a destination without continuous control
Continuous control of direction and speed
Cancellation of lateral physical movement
questions.explanation: Steering-based navigation is a navigation category in which direction and speed are continuously controlled while the user moves from one point to another.

questions.question: Steering-based navigation is divided into which two types?
options: Spatial steering-based and physical steering-based
Gaze-directed and hand-directed
Full gait and gait negation
Target selection and route planning
questions.explanation: Steering-based navigation has spatial steering-based navigation and physical steering-based navigation.

questions.question: In gaze-directed spatial steering-based navigation, how does movement occur?
options: Looking at a target moves the user continuously in that direction
Leaning the body cancels the user's lateral movement
Looking at a target instantly moves the user there
Hand gestures determine the direction of travel
questions.explanation: In gaze-directed spatial steering-based navigation, looking at a target location moves the user continuously in the direction of looking.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of physical steering-based navigation?
options: A VR simulator for cars, boats, and spaceships
A gaze-directed travel technique
A hand-directed travel technique
A body-leaning directed travel technique
questions.explanation: Physical steering-based navigation uses vehicular props or additional hardware, such as VR simulators for cars, boats, and spaceships.

data.text: Steering-based navigation involves continuously controlling direction and speed while moving. This navigation is divided into spatial steering-based navigation, which can be gaze-directed, hand-directed, or body-leaning directed, and physical steering-based navigation, which uses hardware or physical setups.
points: Steering-based navigation involves continuously controlling direction and speed while moving.
Navigation is categorized into spatial and physical steering-based types.
Spatial steering-based navigation includes gaze-directed, hand-directed, and body-leaning directed types.
Physical steering-based navigation involves using hardware or physical setups to control travel in a virtual world.

questions.question: What is the main idea behind selection-based locomotion?
options: The user continuously controls direction and speed while moving
The user selects where to go rather than continuously steering movement
The user's body leaning determines the travel direction
The user manipulates the virtual world's scale with gestures
questions.explanation: Selection-based locomotion lets the user choose the destination instead of continuously specifying how to move there by steering or looking.

questions.question: What are the two types of selection-based locomotion?
options: Target selection-based and route planning-based
Spatial steering-based and physical steering-based
Target teleportation and map dragging
Gaze-directed and body-leaning directed
questions.explanation: Selection-based locomotion is divided into target selection-based locomotion and route planning-based locomotion.

questions.question: In target selection-based locomotion, what happens after the user selects a destination?
options: The virtual viewpoint changes so the user feels moved to the target
The virtual world's scale changes to make the target appear closer
The user continues to steer direction and speed until arriving
The virtual viewpoint changes gradually along a preselected route
questions.explanation: In target selection-based locomotion, the user selects a destination or target, and the virtual viewpoint changes so that the user feels moved to it.

questions.question: How does route planning-based locomotion differ from target selection-based teleportation?
options: The user manipulates objects to change the virtual viewpoint
The user continuously steers direction and speed during movement
The user selects a route to the target rather than only the endpoint
The user selects only the endpoint and the viewpoint jumps instantly
questions.explanation: Route planning-based locomotion selects a route to the target, allowing movement along a path and more granular control than merely teleporting to a target.

questions.question: Which implementation idea for manipulation-based locomotion works by changing the virtual viewpoint when certain objects are moved?
options: The homer technique
The world in miniature metaphor
The go-go technique
Target selection-based teleportation
questions.explanation: In the world in miniature metaphor, moving or manipulating certain objects causes a corresponding change in the virtual viewpoint, as if the user moves.

data.text: Selection-based locomotion involves choosing a destination rather than continuously steering or looking to move. This category includes target selection-based locomotion, which instantly changes the viewpoint, and route planning-based locomotion, which provides more granular and natural movement. Alternatively, manipulation-based locomotion uses gestures to change the viewpoint or the world, such as the world in miniature metaphor where manipulating objects causes a change in the virtual viewpoint.
points: Selection-based locomotion involves choosing a destination rather than continuously steering or looking.
Target selection-based locomotion instantly changes the viewpoint to a selected destination.
Route planning-based locomotion involves selecting a path to provide more granular and natural movement.
Manipulation-based locomotion uses gestures to manipulate the viewpoint or the virtual world.
In the world in miniature metaphor, manipulating certain objects causes a change in the virtual viewpoint.

questions.question: What are the two components of navigation?
options: Steering-based navigation, and selection-based locomotion
Locomotion or travel, and wayfinding
Landmark knowledge, and map knowledge
Rendering, and tracking
questions.explanation: Navigation has a motor component, locomotion or travel, and wayfinding.

questions.question: What does wayfinding refer to?
options: Creating and updating a real-world map while localizing positions
Location awareness, path-finding to a destination, and transferring spatial knowledge to the real world
Continuous control of direction and speed while moving between points
Selecting a target and changing the virtual viewpoint instantly
questions.explanation: Wayfinding involves location awareness, ascertaining a path to a desired destination, and transferring spatial knowledge to the real world.

questions.question: What can happen when an XR environment's design does not support the creation of a mental map?
options: Many problems may occur and the overall user experience deteriorates
A world in miniature display automatically provides the missing spatial knowledge
The user no longer needs to know landmarks or follow procedural knowledge
Locomotion or travel alone becomes sufficient for efficient navigation
questions.explanation: The objective of environment design is to make it easier for the user to build a mental map; without that support, problems may occur and the user experience deteriorates.

questions.question: Which types of spatial knowledge form the essential knowledge base of a wayfinding mental model?
options: Steering-based navigation, selection-based locomotion, and manipulation-based locomotion
Landmark knowledge, procedural knowledge, and topological or map-like knowledge
Translational movement, rotational movement, and panoramic video
Material surface property, physical surface property, and triangular mesh
questions.explanation: The spatial knowledge in a wayfinding mental model consists of landmark knowledge, procedural knowledge, and topological or map-like knowledge.

questions.question: How does breadcrumb support help wayfinding?
options: It uses colors to show multiple paths through a single space
It leaves a trail of markers along a path already followed by predecessors
It specifies directions in two-dimensional or three-dimensional space
It displays the entire virtual world, the current position, and routes in miniature
questions.explanation: Breadcrumb support leaves a trail of markers along a path followed by predecessors, helping users recognize an explored path and avoid getting lost.

data.text: Navigation has two components: locomotion and wayfinding. Wayfinding is a mental model used to build a cognitive map of the surroundings and overall environment. Wayfinding support is essential and can be provided through landmarks, maps, path following, breadcrumbs, and compasses.
points: Navigation has two components: locomotion and wayfinding.
Wayfinding is a mental model used to build a cognitive map of the surroundings and overall environment.
Wayfinding support is essential and can be provided through landmarks, maps, path following, breadcrumbs, and compasses.

questions.question: What is the main goal of interaction for system control?
options: To build a mental model of the virtual surroundings
To select one or more objects from a set of virtual objects
To modify an object's position, orientation, scale, or texture
To issue commands that change the system's state or mode
questions.explanation: Interaction for system control is aimed at issuing commands that change system state or mode, such as launching an application, changing settings, or opening a file.

questions.question: Which of the following is an interactive method for system control?
options: Landmark support using obvious distinct non-mobile objects
Breadcrumb support that leaves markers along a followed path
Path following support that denotes multiple paths by colors
Graphical menus adapted for three-dimensional massive environments
questions.explanation: Adapted graphical menus are listed as an interactive method for system control, whereas breadcrumb, landmark, and path following supports are ways of supporting wayfinding.

questions.question: Which combination lists interactive methods for system control?
options: Physical controllers, menus, voice commands, gesture commands, tools, and multimodal interaction
Selection, manipulation, navigation, and wayfinding
Presence, immersion, cybersickness, and tracking
Locomotion, landmark support, map support, and breadcrumb support
questions.explanation: Methods for system control include physical controllers, graphical menus, voice commands, gesture commands, tools, and multimodal interaction techniques.

data.text: Interaction for system control is an interaction technique whose goal is to issue commands that change system state or mode. These commands are most of the regular operations associated with using any software. Interactive methods for system control include physical controllers, graphical menus, voice commands, gesture commands, tools, and multimodal interaction techniques.
points: Interaction for system control is an interaction technique whose goal is to issue commands that change system state or mode.
Interactive methods for system control include physical controllers, graphical menus, voice commands, gesture commands, tools, and multimodal interaction techniques.

questions.question: How do locomotion and wayfinding work together in navigation through a virtual world, and why is wayfinding support important for user experience?
questions.reference_answer: Navigation in a virtual world includes travel and wayfinding, and locomotion is the motor component that moves the user from one point to another. Wayfinding refers to location awareness and to building a mental model or cognitive map of the surroundings and overall environment. Locomotion or travel support alone is not sufficient, because without suitable wayfinding support the user cannot use travel techniques efficiently or effectively in a complex virtual environment.

questions.question: Why can full gait techniques create a mismatch between physical and virtual movement, and how do partial gait and gait negation techniques handle the user's physical movement?
questions.reference_answer: In full gait techniques, completely free walking is not practical, so walking is restricted in the physical space and translated to any amount of movement in virtual space, creating a mismatch. In partial gait techniques, the user walks in place and specialized devices or active walking interfaces map the in-place walking pattern to different types of virtual movement. In gait negation techniques, a specialized setup cancels lateral movement and keeps the user's physical position fixed before the movement is mapped to virtual navigation.

questions.question: How does target selection-based locomotion differ from route planning-based locomotion, and why can route planning give a more gradual sense of movement?
questions.reference_answer: Target selection-based locomotion lets the user select a destination, and the virtual viewpoint changes so the user feels moved to the target, as in teleportation, map dragging, or the jumper technique. Route planning-based locomotion lets the user select a route to the target rather than only the endpoint. Different viewpoint changes while moving through the selected route make the user feel movement along a path, providing more granular control and slightly more natural movement than target-based teleportation.

questions.question: How is interaction for system control different from navigation and object interaction in an immersive environment?
questions.reference_answer: Object interaction in immersive environments means selecting and manipulating objects that are part of the virtual environment, while navigation means moving from one point to another in the virtual environment. Interaction for system control issues commands that change system state or mode, such as launching an application, changing system settings, or opening a file. It can use physical controllers, graphical menus, voice commands, gesture commands, tools, or multimodal interaction techniques.
